prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer turning away from a wall display (0.8–1.2 m in front in frames 1–2) toward a windowed room (3–4 m away in frames 3–4) before tilting down in frame 5, where a woman stands 1.2–1.8 m ahead, flanked by a clothing rack on the left (0.5–1.0 m) and a white shelving unit about 1 m to her left (viewer's right, at 2.0–2.5 m). In frame 1, the bright foreground highlights a hanger and hand within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.3–0.5 m at the bottom edge), while frame 5 shows the camera wearer's left hand/rack on the far left (0.3–0.5 m) and a dark foreground object at the bottom right (0.5–0.8 m) partially occluding the woman's lower legs, with the rack also within arm's reach of the woman's right hand. Across frames 3 to 4, the woman's head silhouette at the lower center brightens as she moves closer (from roughly 2.5 m to 2.0 m) while facing and looking toward the camera wearer, before her head is cropped above the top edge in frame 5. This map clarifies the continuous 3D separation between the foreground rack, the standing woman, and the shelving unit that blend into dark or overexposed regions in RGB, as well as the slant of the wall during frame 2's fast turn. However, the map is unreliable across the glass windows in frames 3–5—treating distant outdoor trees as a flat plane at the same 3–4 m depth as the window frames—and smears object boundaries during the motion-blurred pan in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates no people or objects during the close wall view and turn in frames 1–2, then detects a woman at the bottom center of frames 3–4 (2.0–2.5 m away, facing and looking toward the camera wearer in front of the window) and her torso and legs in frame 5 (1.2–1.8 m away, facing forward with her head cropped out of view above the frame). In frame 5, it also segments a second partial person mask on the far left within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.3–0.5 m, about 1 m left of the standing woman), separating the foreground arm and clothing area from the standing woman behind and to the right of it. Across frames 3 to 5, the shift from small lower-edge head masks to a large full-height mask tracks the camera tilting down and closing the distance to the woman, while her right hand remains within arm's reach of the unsegmented rack to her right. Compared to RGB alone, the masks clearly delineate human boundaries against dark clothing and cluttered racks in frame 5, but the map completely omits all non-person scene elements—including the hanger within reach in frame 1, the clothing racks, the foreground bag occluding the woman's feet, and the white shelf 1 m to her left. It is also unreliable in frame 3, where it hallucinates an overlapping second person mask on a circular background graphic directly behind the woman's head, and in frame 5, where the left-edge person mask bleeds into adjacent hanging clothes.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty during the wall-facing frames 1–2, then plots yellow facial and shoulder keypoints at the bottom center of frames 3–4 for the woman 2.0–2.5 m away, showing her symmetric eye, nose, and ear landmarks facing and looking toward the camera wearer while her body below the shoulders is cropped out. In frame 5, as the camera tilts down and moves to 1.2–1.8 m from the standing woman, the map renders a detailed magenta right-hand skeleton for her at center-left (about 1.2 m away, reaching within arm's reach of the clothing rack) along with yellow keypoints on the lower-left foreground (0.3–0.6 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and a horizontal yellow segment at the lower right (0.6–0.8 m). The progression from upper-body/head landmarks at the bottom of frames 3–4 to hand and lower-scene keypoints in frame 5 reflects the camera wearer's downward pitch and approach, even as the woman's head moves out of view above the top border. This map makes the exact articulation and finger orientation of the woman's right hand grasping the rack in frame 5 and her head tilt in frames 3–4 much easier to read than in the motion-blurred RGB image. However, pose estimation is highly unreliable in frame 5: it misses the standing woman's entire torso, legs, and left hand (which is visible near her hip), while placing disconnected, spurious yellow body keypoints on the foreground clothing rack and dark bag at the bottom left and right.
